title: Ecosystem Intelligence depends on alignment of parts, not the sum of their individual intelligence
content:
A.0.1.1.2 characterizes a decentralized ecosystem as a single entity acting with a greater or lesser amount of intelligence — and states that this is **not** determined by summing the intelligence of its constituent parts, but by their *alignment*.

The counterintuitive claim is the load-bearing one: "very intelligent, but spiritually misaligned participants in a decentralized ecosystem will actually lower Ecosystem Intelligence." Capability is not merely wasted when misaligned — it is actively subtractive, because a capable actor pursuing goals orthogonal to the ecosystem's purpose can do more damage than an incapable one.

This inverts the usual scaling assumption for decentralized systems, which is that recruiting more capable participants monotonically improves outcomes. If the claim holds, recruiting must be alignment-gated first and capability-gated second, and the entire justification for Alignment Engineering follows: there is no point maximizing participant capability without a mechanism that binds it to purpose.
description: Sky's core premise: intelligent but spiritually misaligned participants actively LOWER a decentralized ecosystem's intelligence, so alignment dominates raw capability.
